newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil prices ease on imports.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil prices ease on imports.

text.p: Edible oil prices eased further in India during the week on sustained arrivals of palm olein from Malaysia, traders and industry officials said on Wednesday.
"Prices are at a low key at the moment due to good arrivals of imported oil," C.M. Amla, a leading New Delhi edible oil trader, said.
Traders said palm olein in the domestic markets was quoted at 26,800 rupees per tonne compared with about 27,500 on June 1. Groundnut oil was quoted at 35,600 to 36,000 rupees, the same as last week.
Industry officials said about 120,000 tonnes of palm olein imports arrived in the month of June compared with normal arrivals of about 70,000 to 100,000 tonnes per month.
They said importers had committed huge quantities of palm olein imports from Malaysia at relatively lower prices as they expected prices to remain high in the domestic markets.
"Now the domestic prices have fallen and importers think they have burnt their fingers," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Traders said Malaysian prices had eased considerably on expectations of a good oil palm crop.
Industry officials said Indian domestic summer oilseed arrivals were almost over except in some regions in the western state of Gujarat.

"Arrivals are continuing in the Saurashtra region," Shah said. He said about 30,000 to 40,000 bags (1 bag = 70 kg) of groundnut in shell was arriving each day in Saurashtra, the main groundnut producing region in Gujarat.
Industry officials said the country would enter a lean period from July onwards, when domesic arrivals dry up.
"Thereafter the price movement of edible oil will depend on the progress of the monsoon," Shah said.
Industry officials expect the 1996/97 oilseeds crop to be about 21.26 million tonnes, up from 20.98 million in the previous season.
Industry officials expect the 1997/98 crop to be about two or three percent higher than in 1996/97.
